newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to tender for 26,000t corn/38,000 beans.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to tender for 26,000t corn/38,000 beans.

text.p: Taiwanese buyers are expected to tender for up to 26,000 tonnes of corn and 38,000 tonnes of soybeans this week, traders said on Monday.
The state-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp will place a tender for some 10,000 tonnes of No.2 yellow corn. Taiwan Sugar officials said the delivery date will be set during the tender.

Taiwan's Hui Shung Group was expected to tender this week for a combined shipment of 16,000 tonnes of corn and 38,000 tonnes of soybeans, traders said. The Hui Shung Group's shipment would be slated for delivery in March.
Taiwan's Flour Mills Association will remain sidelined this week because of ample stocks, an association official said. "Taiwan still has plenty of wheat stocks," the official said.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture crop report, due out on Tuesday, will have little impact on Taiwanese buyers since most have bought their January and February shipments, traders said.
Taiwan's soymeal price on Friday for Taipei delivery was quoted at T$9.40-$9.60 a kg, down from $9.50-9.70 a kg the previous week.
The corn powders price was at T$6.70 per kg for Taipei delivery, down from $6.60-$6.80 a week earlier.
Pacific Northwest freight cost was about US$11.50 per tonne and the Gulf of Mexico was quoted at about $21.00-$22.00 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized February shipments.
The local flour price on Friday remains unchanged at T$14.55 to T$15.68 a kg for Taipei delivery.
